se-apathy-1.explanation: Four elections of falling turnout is disengagement, and apathy and torpor both name that listless lack of interest; zeal and alacrity say the opposite.
se-apathy-1.stem: Turnout fell for the fourth election running, and the council blamed the weather rather than the _____ its own decisions had produced.

se-archaic-1.explanation: Needing a nineteenth-century dictionary dates the wording to an earlier era, which archaic and antiquated both say and nascent and novel deny.
se-archaic-1.stem: The statute's language is so _____ that clerks must consult a nineteenth-century dictionary to work out what two of its clauses forbid.

se-arduous-1.explanation: Nine years for one ceiling is the measure of effort the blank needs, and arduous and laborious both describe work demanding sustained hard labour.
se-arduous-1.stem: Restoring the frescoes proved far more _____ than the estimate had suggested: two conservators spent nine years on a single chapel ceiling.

se-assuage-1.explanation: The residents are packing anyway, so the broadcast failed to calm them; assuage and allay both mean to soothe a fear rather than stir one up.
se-assuage-1.stem: The governor's evening broadcast did nothing to _____ the fears of residents downstream, who had already begun loading their cars.

se-bolster-1.explanation: Fresh finds agreeing with an old proposal strengthen it, and bolster and buttress both mean to shore up a claim rather than attack or weaken it.
se-bolster-1.stem: Each new excavation season produced pottery that served to _____ the dating the team had proposed a decade earlier.

se-denigrate-1.explanation: Attacking the person instead of answering the question is blackening a reputation, which denigrate and malign both say and the praising options reverse.
se-denigrate-1.stem: Rivals found it easier to _____ the architect than to explain why their own proposals had been rejected twice.

se-elicit-1.explanation: The picture has to draw the feeling out of an uninformed viewer, and elicit and evoke both mean to call up a response rather than suppress or prevent one.
se-elicit-1.stem: The photograph was chosen because it would _____ the same unease in a viewer who knew nothing about where it had been taken.

se-esoteric-1.explanation: If neighbouring specialists struggle, the material is understood by only a few; esoteric and abstruse both carry that obscurity, while lucid and pedestrian contradict it.
se-esoteric-1.stem: The journal's reputation rests on articles so _____ that even specialists in the neighbouring subfield read them with real difficulty.

se-loquacious-1.explanation: Abandoning a book before the second station is the effect of a passenger who will not stop talking, and loquacious and garrulous both leave him equally talkative.
se-loquacious-1.stem: Seated beside the most _____ passenger on the train, she gave up on her book somewhere before the second station.

se-morose-1.explanation: Silent dinners and early exits describe settled gloom, and morose and saturnine both name a sullen, darkened temperament rather than a cheerful one.
se-morose-1.stem: After the verdict he grew _____, sitting through dinners without speaking and leaving before the plates were cleared.

se-onerous-1.explanation: A decade of work spent chiefly on repayment marks the terms as a heavy burden, and onerous and arduous both leave them equally punishing.
se-onerous-1.stem: The terms of the loan proved so _____ that the family spent the next decade working chiefly to meet them.

se-opaque-1.explanation: Needing a commentary to follow one paragraph says the prose cannot be seen through, and opaque and impenetrable both leave it equally hard to read.
se-opaque-1.stem: The prose of the founding charter is _____ to modern readers, who need a commentary open beside it to follow a single paragraph.

se-paragon-1.explanation: A man held up for thirty years as what public service should look like is a model of it, and paragon and exemplar both leave him the ideal case.
se-paragon-1.stem: For thirty years the school held him up as the _____ of public service, which made the later disclosures land all the harder.

se-precarious-1.explanation: Unsigned factions and quiet rearmament make the ceasefire unstable, and precarious and tenuous both leave it liable to collapse.
se-precarious-1.stem: The ceasefire was _____ from the first week: two of the five factions had signed nothing at all, and the rest were quietly rearming.

se-rescind-1.explanation: A licence withdrawn under pressure is being cancelled by the body that issued it, which rescind and annul both mean; perpetuate would keep it in force.
se-rescind-1.stem: Under pressure from three states, the board voted to _____ the licence it had granted only eleven weeks earlier.

se-soporific-1.explanation: An audience that stops taking notes and starts watching the clock is being put to sleep, and soporific and somnolent both say the talk induced sleepiness.
se-soporific-1.stem: The keynote was so _____ that by the second graph a third of the audience had stopped taking notes and begun checking the time.

se-tirade-1.explanation: Forty minutes of attack on three targets at once is a sustained verbal assault, which is what a tirade and a broadside both are.
se-tirade-1.stem: What was billed as a closing statement turned into a forty-minute _____ against the agency, the press and his own lawyers.

se-turgid-1.explanation: Three pages of tribute against a one-sentence announcement marks the writing as inflated, and turgid and bombastic both leave it pompously overblown.
se-turgid-1.stem: Three pages of _____ tribute preceded the actual announcement, which when it finally arrived took a single sentence.

tc-advocate-1.explanation: Being first to put the case for removal is public support for it, which advocate names; proscribe, decry and denounce would all be arguing against.
tc-advocate-1.stem: Having spent a decade studying the river, she was the first hydrologist to _____ removing the dam rather than repairing it again.

tc-amalgamate-1.explanation: Three bodies becoming one institute with one budget is combination rather than replacement or demotion, and amalgamate is the word for merging into a single whole.
tc-amalgamate-1.stem: Rather than let three rival societies go on duplicating each other's work, the trustees voted to _____ them into a single institute with one budget.

tc-ascetic-1.explanation: One meal, no heat and an hour of speech a week is severe self-denial practised for spiritual ends, which ascetic names and the four opulent options contradict.
tc-ascetic-1.stem: The order's _____ regime allowed one meal a day, no heating in the cells, and a single hour of conversation each week.

tc-attenuate-1.explanation: A shock arriving as a faint tremor is force reduced on the way, which is what attenuate means; the other options would make it worse or start it.
tc-attenuate-1.stem: Each layer of foam was there to _____ the vibration, so that what finally reached the instruments was a faint tremor rather than a shock.

tc-burnish-1.explanation: A reputation that has been dulled and a book meant to fix it calls for polishing, and burnish is the verb for restoring a shine to a name.
tc-burnish-1.stem: The memoir's real purpose was to _____ a reputation that two decades of litigation and unflattering testimony had steadily dulled.

tc-castigate-1.explanation: Going beyond noting failures to attack at length is severe criticism, which castigate supplies; the other verbs excuse or soothe rather than rebuke.
tc-castigate-1.stem: The report does not merely note the failures; it goes on to _____ the department at length for ignoring warnings it had itself commissioned.

tc-cavalier-1.explanation: A glance, a shrug and a signature is dismissive handling of something serious, which is what cavalier names; the other options describe care, not carelessness.
tc-cavalier-1.stem: His _____ treatment of the safety checklist, a glance and a shrug and a signature, was what the inquiry eventually fixed on.

tc-censure-1.explanation: A penalty just short of expulsion, entered into the record, is official disapproval: censure. Approbation and deference would be praise or respect instead.
tc-censure-1.stem: The committee stopped short of expulsion, settling on a formal _____ that was read into the record and published the same afternoon.

tc-coalesce-1.explanation: Four groups becoming one organisation is the clue: coalesce is the merging into a whole, where polarize would split them and attenuate would thin them out.
tc-coalesce-1.stem: What began as four unconnected tenant groups had, by the spring, begun to _____ into a single organisation with one set of demands.

tc-commensurate-1.explanation: A year's wages set against a whole career is a failure of proportion, and commensurate is the word for matching in size or degree.
tc-commensurate-1.stem: The settlement was never _____ with the harm done: a single year's wages for a career that had ended at thirty-one.

tc-construe-1.explanation: Treating silence as though it meant consent is an act of interpretation, which is what construe names; the others assign blame, reject, outline or cancel.
tc-construe-1.stem: The lawyers warned that a court would _____ the silence as consent, which is why every concession had to be read aloud and minuted.

tc-dearth-1.explanation: The sentence contrasts money, of which there was plenty, with a missing willingness to decide, so the blank needs the word for a shortage, dearth.
tc-dearth-1.stem: What stalled the project was not a _____ of money but of anyone willing to say out loud which of the four designs was best.

tc-deleterious-1.explanation: Harm that only shows after eleven years is damage done gradually, which is exactly what deleterious describes; benign and innocuous say the opposite.
tc-deleterious-1.stem: The additive passed every short-term trial; only after eleven years of use did its _____ effect on the liver become undeniable.

tc-demur-1.explanation: Thanking the board while pleading inexperience is a polite refusal, not a surrender or an evasion, and demur is the word for objecting courteously.
tc-demur-1.stem: Offered the chairmanship in front of the whole board, she began to _____, thanking them warmly and pleading an inexperience that nobody present believed in.

tc-disinterested-1.explanation: No client, no stake and nothing to gain is the definition of impartiality, and disinterested is the word for a judgement no interest can bend.
tc-disinterested-1.stem: Both sides agreed to abide by the finding of referees who were _____: no client in the room, no stake in the outcome, nothing to gain either way.

tc-estimable-1.explanation: Hardworking, honest and widely liked is a man who deserves respect, which is what estimable says; the other options are faults rather than virtues.
tc-estimable-1.stem: His predecessor had been in every way _____, hardworking and honest and widely liked, which made the decision to replace him harder to explain.

tc-exculpate-1.explanation: Evidence putting him in another city clears him of the charge rather than damaging him, and exculpate is the verb for freeing someone from blame.
tc-exculpate-1.stem: The new timestamps did not merely cast doubt on the charge; they _____ him outright, placing him in another city on the evening in question.

tc-fawn-1.explanation: Worst ideas going unchallenged is the consequence of servile flattery rather than criticism, and fawn is the verb for praising a superior that way.
tc-fawn-1.stem: New arrivals learned quickly to _____ over the director's every passing remark, which is why his worst ideas went unchallenged for years.

tc-flag-1.explanation: A fourth hour and a break called in response point to energy running down, which is what flag means; the other verbs describe growth or a surge.
tc-flag-1.stem: By the fourth hour of rehearsal the choir's attention had begun to _____, and the conductor called a break rather than fight it.

tc-foment-1.explanation: Pamphlets aimed at unrest rather than explanation are there to stir it up, which foment names; the other verbs would calm the towns instead.
tc-foment-1.stem: The pamphlets printed in the back room were meant to _____ unrest in the garrison towns, not to explain any particular grievance.

tc-fractious-1.explanation: Shouting down the chair and walking out is quarrelsome unruliness, which is what fractious describes, and the surprise of June's unanimity depends on it.
tc-fractious-1.stem: A committee that had been _____ all spring, shouting down its own chair and walking out twice, somehow produced a unanimous report in June.

tc-iconoclast-1.explanation: Someone hired to dismantle cherished traditions is an iconoclast; a sycophant would flatter them and a pundit would merely comment on them.
tc-iconoclast-1.stem: Hired to shake the place up, the new director turned out to be exactly the _____ the board had feared, dismantling in one year the traditions it had spent three decades defending.

tc-indolent-1.explanation: Arriving early and waiting is offered as proof against laziness, so the blank has to be the accusation being denied, which is indolent.
tc-indolent-1.stem: The staff were not _____ so much as unled: they arrived early, sat down at their desks, and waited for instructions that never came.

tc-intimate-1.explanation: Never saying it outright but conveying it with an eyebrow and a pause is hinting, and intimate is the verb for suggesting something indirectly.
tc-intimate-1.stem: He would never say outright that the figures had been altered; he preferred to _____ it, with a raised eyebrow and a pause in the right place.

tc-invidious-1.explanation: The resentment left on every rung is the clue: the exercise is not harmless but actively provoking, which is what invidious means.
tc-invidious-1.stem: Ranking colleagues by a single number is deeply _____: whatever the final list shows, it leaves resentment standing on every rung below the top.

tc-itinerant-1.explanation: Six weeks here and a term there, never twice in one town, is a working life spent travelling, which is what itinerant describes.
tc-itinerant-1.stem: For thirty years he was an _____ lecturer, six weeks at one college and a term at the next, never twice in the same town in a single year.

tc-officious-1.explanation: Going past helpful into unasked-for interference and correction is officious; obsequious would mean flattering the guests rather than overruling them.
tc-officious-1.stem: The porter was not merely helpful but _____, rearranging luggage nobody had asked him to touch and correcting the guests' pronunciation of the street names.

tc-opaque-1.explanation: A clause its own drafters cannot explain is impossible to see through, which is what opaque says; lucid, patent and cogent all mean the reverse.
tc-opaque-1.stem: The charter's key clause is so _____ that even the two lawyers who drafted it cannot explain its effect without resorting to a diagram.

tc-pragmatic-1.explanation: The contrast between an ideal city and what can be built by spring is the clue: she is judging by what works rather than by theory, which is what pragmatic names.
tc-pragmatic-1.stem: Her approach to the housing shortage was resolutely _____: she asked not what an ideal city would look like, but what could actually be built by spring.

tc-sinecure-1.explanation: A title and an office with no duties attached is precisely a sinecure, a position that pays without asking for work.
tc-sinecure-1.stem: The post came with a title, a corner office and no duty anyone could name, a _____ invented to keep a difficult man out of the way of the work.

tc-sporadic-1.explanation: Three meetings one month and none the next describes an irregular pattern rather than a hasty or difficult one, which is what sporadic says.
tc-sporadic-1.stem: The committee's meetings were so _____ that summer, three in May and none at all in June, that nobody could remember what had last been decided.

tc-trenchant-1.explanation: Two sentences succeeding where forty pages failed points to criticism that is sharp and effective, which is what trenchant names.
tc-trenchant-1.stem: Two sentences of her review did what forty pages of committee prose had not: the criticism was _____ enough to end the project that same afternoon.
